h: Passing Through Waters and Fire with Hashem
The promise of divine accompaniment illuminates the passage from fear and spiritual danger toward protection.
Divine Presence in the Waters and Fire of Exile

p: "גַּם כִּי אֵלֵךְ וְגוֹמֵר לֹא אִירָא רָע כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי".
— 'Even though I walk, etc., I will fear no evil, for You are with me.'
זֶה שֶׁאָמַר הַכָּתוּב בַּהַפְטָרָה:
— This is what Scripture declares in the Haftarah:
"כִּי תַעֲבֹר בַּמַּיִם אִתְּךָ אָנִי, וּבַנְּהָרוֹת לֹא יִשְׁטְפוּךָ,
— 'When you pass through the waters, I am with you; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow you;
כִּי תֵלֵךְ בְּמוֹ אֵשׁ לֹא תִכָּוֶה וְגוֹמֵר".
— when you walk through fire, you shall not be scorched, etc.'
וְיֵשׁ לְהָבִין: וְכִי מִי עוֹבֵר בַּמַּיִם וּבָאֵשׁ?
— And one must understand: does anyone literally pass through water and fire?
וּכְשֶׁעָבְרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּיָּם וּבַיַּרְדֵּן
— And when Israel traversed the Sea and the Jordan,
עָבְרוּ בְּנֵס בַּיַּבָּשָׁה!
— they crossed through a miracle upon dry land!
וְכֵן חֲנַנְיָה, מִישָׁאֵל וַעֲזַרְיָה הוּשְׁלְכוּ לָאֵשׁ
— And likewise Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah were cast into the fire
וְלֹא הָלְכוּ בָּאֵשׁ!
— and did not walk through fire!
אַךְ הַכָּתוּב מְרַמֵּז עַל שְׁתֵּי הַקְּלִיפּוֹת: עֵשָׂו וְיִשְׁמָעֵאל,
— Rather, Scripture alludes to the two impure husks (kelipot): Esau and Ishmael,
שֶׁהֵם שָׁרְשֵׁי כָּל שִׁבְעִים הַקְּלִיפּוֹת.
— which are the generative roots of all seventy kelipot.
וּכְנֶגֶד מַיִם – חֲסָדִים דִּקְדוּשָׁה,
— And corresponding to water—the holy emanations of Lovingkindness (Chasadim)—
יֵשׁ לְעֻמַּת זֶה קְלִיפַּת יִשְׁמָעֵאל,
— there exists parallel to this the kelipah of Ishmael,
שֶׁהוּא תַּאֲוַות וְחֶמְדַּת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, מַיִם הַזֵּידוֹנִים.
— which is the lust and physical appetite of this world, the 'raging waters.'
וּכְנֶגֶד אֵשׁ – גְּבוּרוֹת דִּקְדוּשָׁה,
— And corresponding to fire—the holy emanations of Might (Gevurot)—
הוּא לְעֻמַּת זֶה קְלִיפַּת עֵשָׂו,
— there exists parallel to this the kelipah of Esau,
שֶׁהוּא הַקִּנְאָה וּרְצִיחָה.
— which is jealousy and murder.
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר הַנָּבִיא
— And regarding this the prophet stated
שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יַעֲזוֹר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל מִשְּׁתֵּי הַקְּלִיפּוֹת:
— that Hashem, blessed be He, will rescue Israel from these two kelipot:
שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁטְפוּךָ מַיִם הַזֵּידוֹנִים,
— that the raging waters shall not overflow you,
וְלֹא תִבְעַר בְּךָ אֵשׁ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו.
— and the fire of Esau shall not scorch you.
וְאָמַר הַכָּתוּב: "כִּי אֲנִי ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ וְגוֹמֵר מוֹשִׁיעֶךָ",
— And Scripture states: 'For I am Hashem your God, etc., your Savior,'
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כא):
— in the manner of what is written in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah, Parashah 21):
"יִשְׁעִי" בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים,
— 'My salvation'—on Yom Kippur,
שֶׁהוּא מְחִילַת עֲווֹנוֹת לְתַקֵּן הֶעָבָר אַחַר שֶׁקִּלְקֵל.
— which is the forgiveness of iniquities to repair the past after one has stumbled.
"נָתַתִּי כָפְרְךָ מִצְרַיִם"
— 'I gave Egypt as your ransom'—
אָמַר לְשׁוֹן עָבָר,
— stated in the past tense,
דְּקָאֵי עַל גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם,
— for it refers to the exile of Egypt,
שֶׁמַּה שֶּׁנָּתַן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּלֵב פַּרְעֹה וְעַמּוֹ לִרְדּוֹף אַחֲרֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
— wherein what Hashem placed in the heart of Pharaoh and his people to pursue Israel,
אַף שֶׁכְּבָר שִׁלְּחוּם וּבִקְּשׁוּ מֵהֶם שֶׁיֵּצְאוּ,
— even though they had already dispatched them and pleaded with them to depart,
הָיָה מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָיָה עוֹד קִטְרוּג עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
— was because there still remained an accusatory indictment against Israel,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בַּמְּכִילְתָּא:
— as stated in the Mekhilta:
"'וְהַמַּיִם לָהֶם חֹמָה' – כְּתִיב חָסֵר,
— 'And the water was a wall (chomah) unto them'—written defectively without a vav (chemah),
שֶׁנִּתְמַלֵּא עֲלֵיהֶם חֵימָה".
— indicating that supernal wrath was stirred against them.
וּבַמִּדְרָשׁ (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כא)
— And in the Midrash (Shemot Rabbah, Parashah 21)
שֶׁהָיָה קִטְרוּג עֲלֵיהֶם בַּיָּם: "הַלָּלוּ וְכוּלֵי".
— that there was an indictment against them at the Sea: 'These are idolaters, etc.'
וּלְזֶה נָתַן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּלֵב פַּרְעֹה שֶׁיִּרְדְּפוּ אַחֲרֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
— And for this, Hashem placed in the heart of Pharaoh that they pursue Israel,
וְהָיָה הַמִּשְׁפָּט שֶׁנִּטְבְּעוּ בַּיָּם
— and the judgment fell that the Egyptians were drowned in the sea,
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁבֵּירֵר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
— because Hashem clarified
שֶׁכָּל מַה שֶּׁיֵּשׁ טַעֲנוֹת עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
— that all allegations held against Israel
הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי הָרָע שֶׁנִּמְצָא בְּמִצְרַיִם,
— derived solely through the ambient evil present in Egypt,
וּמִזֶּה הִכְנִיסוּ הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָה בְּלֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל גַּם כֵּן.
— and from that they introduced the 'leaven in the dough' into the hearts of Israel as well.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "נָתַתִּי כָפְרְךָ מִצְרָיִם".
— And this is why Scripture states: 'I gave Egypt as your ransom.'
וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָמַר הַכָּתוּב: "כּוּשׁ וּסְבָא תַּחְתֶּיךָ",
— And afterwards Scripture states: 'Cush and Seba in your stead,'
נִרְאֶה שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז עַל מִלְחֶמֶת זֶרַח הַכּוּשִׁי עַל אָסָא (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים ב יד),
— which appears to allude to the war of Zerach the Cushite against Asa (II Chronicles 14),
שֶׁהוּזְכַּר שָׁם חַיִל אֶלֶף אֲלָפִים,
— wherein an army of a million warriors is mentioned,
וְלֹא מָצִינוּ חַיִל כָּבֵד כָּזֶה.
— and we find no such massive opposing force elsewhere.
וּכְבָר אָמַרְנוּ שֶׁכֹּחַ אוּמָּה לְמִלְחָמָה
— And we have already explained that a nation's military power
הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם טַעֲנָה וְקִטְרוּג חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
— stems solely from their possessing an accusatory claim, Heaven forbid,
שֶׁנִּמְצָא גַּם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מֵעֵין קְלִיפָּה שֶׁלָּהֶם,
— that there exists within Israel a trace of their specific kelipah,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִתְגַּבְּרִין.
— and through that leverage they become empowered.
וּקְלִיפַּת כּוּשׁ הוּא פְּגַם הַבְּרִית,
— And the kelipah of Cush is the blemish of the Covenant (immorality),
שֶׁבָּא מֵחָם שֶׁשִּׁמֵּשׁ בַּתֵּיבָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין קח:) וְלָקָה בְּעוֹרוֹ,
— originating from Ham who cohabited in the Ark (Sanhedrin 108b) and was stricken in his skin,
וְזֶה הָיָה פְּגַם הַבְּרִית כֵּיוָן שֶׁנֶּאֱסַר לָהֶם בַּתֵּיבָה,
— and this was a breach of the Covenant since cohabitation was forbidden to them in the Ark,
וְכֵן יֵשׁ מַאן דְּאָמַר רְבָעוֹ.
— and there is also an opinion that he sodomized him.
וְכוּשׁ בְּכוֹרוֹ שֶׁל חָם, וּסְבָא בְּכוֹרוֹ שֶׁל כּוּשׁ,
— And Cush was the firstborn of Ham, and Seba the firstborn of Cush;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁבִּקְדוּשָׁה הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַקְּדוּשָׁה בִּבְכוֹרוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
— and just as in the realm of holiness the holy root rests in the firstborn of Israel,
כֵּן בָּהֶם עִיקַּר הַזּוּהֲמָא בַּבְּכוֹרוֹת,
— so among them the prime defilement is concentrated in the firstborn;
וּלְזֶה כּוּשׁ וּסְבָא שׁוֹרֶשׁ קְלִיפַּת פְּגַם הַבְּרִית.
— and for this reason Cush and Seba are the generative root of the kelipah of covenantal blemish.
וּמִסְּתָמָא הָיָה אָז טַעֲנָה עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּעִנְיָן זֶה,
— And presumably there was then an indictment against Israel in this realm,
וְהִתְעוֹרְרוּ לְהִלָּחֵם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
— and they were aroused to wage war against Israel;
וְהִתְפַּלֵּל אָסָא:
— and Asa prayed:
"עָזְרֵנוּ ה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ כִּי עָלֶיךָ נִשְׁעַנּוּ וּבְשִׁמְךָ בָאנוּ וְגוֹמֵר",
— 'Help us, Hashem our God, for upon You we rely, and in Your Name we have come, etc.'
וְאָז נֶהֶרְגוּ הֵם בַּמַּגֵּפָה וְהָיוּ כֹּפֶר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
— and then they were slain in a plague and became a ransom for Israel,
שֶׁבֵּירֵר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁמֵּהַקְּלִיפָּה שֶׁנִּמְצָא בָּהֶם
— in that Hashem clarified that from the kelipah residing in them
נִכְנַס הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָה בְּלֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל,
— the leaven in the dough had penetrated into the hearts of Israel;
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כּוּשׁ וּסְבָא תַּחְתֶּיךָ".
— and this is what is stated: 'Cush and Seba in your stead.'
וְאָמַר: "מֵאֲשֶׁר יָקַרְתָּ בְעֵינַי נִכְבַּדְתָּ",
— And Scripture says: 'Since you were precious in My sight, you have been honored,'
וְאִיתָא (זֹהַר חָדָשׁ בָּלָק):
— and it is stated (Zohar Chadash, Balak):
"יָקָר מִבָּעֵי לֵיהּ וְכוּלֵי, מַהוּ יָקַרְתָּ? מִכְּלָל דְּאִיהוּ מִגַּרְמֵיהּ אִתְיַקַּר וְכוּלֵי,
— 'It should have said "you are precious" (yakar); what is "you became precious" (yakarta)? It implies that he made himself precious through his own effort, etc.,
וַאֲנִי אֲהַבְתִּיךָ, דְּהָא לֵית רְחִימוּ לְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא בַּהֲדֵי בַּר נָשׁ בְּעָלְמָא אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּתָב מֵחוֹבֵיהּ וְכוּלֵי,
— and I have loved you, for there is no divine love for any man in the world except for one who repents of his sins, etc.,
אֲבָל מָה אֶעֱבֵיד דְּהָא יְהֵיבַת רְשׁוּ וְכוּלֵי",
— yet what shall I do, seeing that permission was given, etc.,'
"וְאֶתֵּן אָדָם תַּחְתֶּיךָ" – אַל תִּקְרֵי אָדָם אֶלָּא אֱדוֹם;
— 'and I will give Adam in your stead'—do not read Adam, but Edom;
וְכֵן דָּרַשׁ "וּלְאֻמִּים" עַל עֵשָׂו,
— and so it expounded 'and nations' (u-le'umim) as referring to Esau,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וּלְאֹם מִלְאֹם יֶאֱמָץ".
— mirroring the verse: 'and the one nation shall be stronger than the other nation.'
וְזֶה נֶאֱמַר בֶּעָתִיד,
— And this is stated in the future tense,
שֶׁכֵּן מֵכִין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְכָל בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה כֹּפֶר נֶפֶשׁ
— for so does Hashem prepare for every penitent a soul-ransom
מַה שֶּׁיֵּשׁ כְּנֶגְדּוֹ בַּקְּלִיפָּה,
— from that which exists parallel to him in the kelipah,
כְּעִנְיַן מַה שֶׁכָּתַב הָאֲרִ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
— in the manner of what the holy Ari of blessed memory wrote
בְּמַה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "נוֹטֵל חֶלְקוֹ וְחֵלֶק חֲבֵירוֹ וְכוּלֵי",
— on the teaching: 'he receives his portion and the portion of his counterpart, etc.,'
וְהַיְינוּ מִי שֶׁהוּא כְּנֶגְדּוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ נִיצוֹץ טוֹב הַנּוֹגֵעַ לְנַפְשׁוֹ.
— meaning the one standing opposite him who contains a holy spark pertaining to his soul.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כִּי תַעֲבֹר בַּמַּיִם אִתְּךָ אָנִי וְגוֹמֵר",
— And this is what Scripture states: 'When you pass through the waters, I am with you, etc.,'
"כִּי תֵלֵךְ בְּמוֹ אֵשׁ לֹא תִכָּוֶה"
— and 'when you walk through fire, you shall not be scorched'—
וְלֹא כְתִיב "אִתְּךָ אָנִי".
— and it is not written here 'I am with you.'
וְהוּא שֶׁמִּקְּלִיפַּת עֵשָׂו, שֶׁהִיא הָרְצִיחָה וְהַכַּעַס,
— And this is because from the kelipah of Esau, which is murder and anger,
לֹא יוּשְׁאַר מְאוּמָה לֶעָתִיד,
— nothing whatever will remain in the ultimate future,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְלֹא יִהְיֶה שָׂרִיד לְבֵית עֵשָׂו".
— as it is stated: 'And there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau.'
וְאָמַר הַכָּתוּב: "לֹא תִכָּוֶה וְלֶהָבָה לֹא תִבְעַר בָּךְ",
— And Scripture states: 'you shall not be scorched, neither shall the flame burn upon you,'
עַל פִּי מַה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וּבֵית יוֹסֵף לֶהָבָה וּבֵית עֵשָׂו לְקַשׁ".
— based upon what is stated: 'and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble.'
"לֹא תִבְעַר בָּךְ" – אֲבָל יִשְׂרְפוּ אֶת עֵשָׂו,
— 'It shall not burn upon you'—yet they will consume Esau in fire,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כִּי הִנֵּה הַיּוֹם בָּא בֹּעֵר כַּתַּנּוּר וְהָיוּ וְגוֹמֵר קַשׁ,
— and as it is stated: 'For behold, the day comes, burning as an oven, and all the proud shall be stubble,
וְלִהַט אֹתָם הַיּוֹם הַבָּא וְגוֹמֵר אֲשֶׁר לֹא יַעֲזֹב לָהֶם שֹׁרֶשׁ וְעָנָף",
— and the day that comes shall burn them up, that it shall leave them neither root nor branch,'
וְזֶהוּ "לֹא יִהְיֶה שָׂרִיד לְבֵית עֵשָׂו".
— and this is 'there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau.'
וְהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שֶׁלָּהֶם הוּא אֵשׁ שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם
— And their evil inclination is the very fire of Gehenna
וּמְלַהֶטֶת אוֹתָם,
— and it consumes them,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בַּמִּדְרָשׁ:
— as stated in the Midrash:
"אֵשׁ שֶׁיּוֹצְאָה מִגּוּפָן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים וּמְלַהֶטֶת אוֹתָם,
— "A fire that emerges from the body of the wicked and consumes them;
מַאי טַעְמָא? דִּכְתִיב: 'רוּחֲכֶם אֵשׁ תֹּאכַלְכֶם'".
— what is the reason? For it is written: 'Your breath, as fire, shall devour you.'"
וְהִיא אֵשׁ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע.
— And this is the fire of the evil inclination.
וְזֶהוּ "לֹא תִבְעַר בָּךְ" – אֲבָל יִבְעַר בָּהֶם.
— And this is 'it shall not burn upon you'—yet it will burn within them.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן נֶגֶד קְלִיפַּת יִשְׁמָעֵאל,
— In contrast regarding the kelipah of Ishmael,
דְּאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג, קלח עַמּוּד א):
— for it is brought in the holy Zohar (Part III, 138a):
"אִצְטְרִיךְ יֵצֶר הָרָע לְעָלְמָא וְכוּלֵי,
— "The evil inclination is necessary for the world, etc.,
דְּאִלְמָלֵא יֵצֶר הָרָע חֶדְוָותָא דִּשְׁמַעְתְּתָא לָא לֶיהֱוֵי".
— for without the evil inclination there would be no passionate joy in Torah study."
וְאַף לֶעָתִיד יוּשְׁאַר יֵצֶר וְחֵשֶׁק זֶה,
— And even in the ultimate future this drive and passion will remain,
רַק דְּאִתְלַבַּן מֵרִשְׁעוֹי.
— only that it will be purified of its wickedness.
עַל זֶה אָמַר: "כִּי תַעֲבֹר בַּמַּיִם אִתְּךָ אָנִי",
— Concerning this Scripture states: 'When you pass through the waters, I am with you,'
שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יְבָרֵר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַחֵשֶׁק לַחֲמִידוּ דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא.
— for Hashem will refine it so that all passion is channeled into the delight of the Torah.
"וּבַנְּהָרוֹת לֹא יִשְׁטְפוּךָ" – מַיִם הַזֵּידוֹנִים,
— 'And through the rivers, they shall not overflow you'—referring to the raging waters,
רַק שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה יִזְכֶּה לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
— only that through this he will merit words of Torah.
וְכֵן דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
— And so too King David, peace be upon him,
שֶׁנִּכְתַּב עָלָיו שֶׁפָּגַם בְּעִנְיָן זֶה,
— concerning whom it was written that he stumbled in this matter,
שֶׁתָּלוּ בוֹ כְּדֵי לְהוֹרוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה
— which was attributed to him solely to teach the path of repentance,
שֶׁאִם חָטָא יָחִיד וְכוּלֵי (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ה.),
— that if an individual sins, etc. (Avodah Zarah 5a),
אָמַר: "גַּם כִּי אֵלֵךְ בְּגֵיא צַלְמָוֶת לֹא אִירָא רָע",
— proclaimed: 'Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil,'
וְהַיְינוּ פְּגָם זֶה שֶׁנִּקְרָא רָע
— meaning this specific blemish which is titled 'evil'
בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א, ריט עַמּוּד ב) וּבַגְּמָרָא (נִדָּה יג.);
— in the holy Zohar (Part I, 219b) and in the Gemara (Niddah 13a);
"כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי"
— 'for You are with me'—
כְּעִנְיַן מַה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כִּי תַעֲבֹר בַּמַּיִם אִתְּךָ אָנִי".
— mirroring the verse: 'When you pass through the waters, I am with you.'
"שִׁבְטְךָ וּמִשְׁעַנְתֶּךָ הֵמָּה יְנַחֲמֻנִי"
— 'Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me'—
וְהוּא מַה שֶּׁמָּצִינוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין קז.):
— and this reflects what we find (Sanhedrin 107a):
"קַבֵּל עָלֶיךָ יִסּוּרִין",
— 'Accept afflictions upon yourself,'
וְזֶהוּ "שִׁבְטְךָ" שֶׁמֵּרִים הַשֵּׁבֶט;
— and this is 'Your rod' when He raises the rod of chastisement;
"וּמִשְׁעַנְתֶּךָ" – שֶׁנַּעֲשֶׂה מִזֶּה מִשְׁעֶנֶת,
— 'and Your staff'—that out of this a support is fashioned,
שֶׁנִּדְרַשׁ עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (חֲגִיגָה יד.),
— which is expounded as referring to words of Torah, as stated (Chagigah 14a),
"הֵמָּה יְנַחֲמֻנִי".
— 'they comfort me.'
וְיִהְיֶה הַתּוֹעֶלֶת מִזֶּה:
— And the ultimate fruit of this will be:
"וְשַׁבְתִּי בְּבֵית ה' לְאֹרֶךְ יָמִים",
— 'and I shall dwell in the house of Hashem for length of days,'
שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה כָּל בַּקָּשָׁתוֹ:
— for this was his entire yearning:
"שִׁבְתִּי בְּבֵית ה' כָּל יְמֵי חַיַּי",
— 'that I may dwell in the house of Hashem all the days of my life,'
שֶׁבְּשַׁבָּת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל יוֹשְׁבִין בְּבֵית ה' בְּהֵיכָלָא דְּמַלְכָּא.
— for on Shabbat all Israel dwell in the house of Hashem, in the palace of the King.
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר: "אַחַת שָׁאַלְתִּי וְגוֹמֵר שִׁבְתִּי בְּבֵית ה' כָּל יְמֵי חַיַּי".
— And concerning this he declared: 'One thing have I asked, etc., that I may dwell in the house of Hashem all the days of my life.'
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר "כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי",
— And over this he said 'for You are with me,'
שֶׁיְּהֵא נַעֲשֶׂה מֵהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע חֲמִידוּ דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא,
— that from the evil inclination there shall be made a passionate longing for Torah,
"וְשַׁבְתִּי בְּבֵית ה' לְאֹרֶךְ יָמִים".
— 'and I shall dwell in the house of Hashem for length of days.'

paragraphs.text: Zohar Chadash, Balak 37: “Rabbi Elazar opened and said: “Since you became precious in My eyes, you were honored, and I loved you; I will give a man in your place and peoples in exchange for your life.” Instead of “you became precious,” it should say “precious”: “Because you are precious in My eyes.” What does “you became precious” mean? It implies that he made himself precious. This is indeed so: Anyone guilty before the Holy One, blessed be He, is initially despised and an abomination before Him. After he reconsiders and repents of his sin, he makes himself precious. The Holy One, blessed be He, addresses him and says, “Since you became precious”—you made yourself precious.”

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 44:1: “One who has a great longing for bodily desires should not become distressed and think how damaged he is to have such great longing. On the contrary, he is a vessel prepared for the intensity of love and the longing to seek truth. This is how that elder consoled Abaye (Sukkah 52a). (According to some commentators in Tosafot, at the beginning of Chullin (6a), that elder was Eliyahu. I heard that this is indeed the truth; this is not the place to address Tosafot’s difficulty there.) Concerning this they said that in the future the evil inclination appears to the righteous like a mountain, and to the wicked like a strand of hair. There is no falsehood here: both are true, for the former’s longing and desire are exceedingly powerful.”

paragraphs.text: Avodah Zarah 5a:2: “The Gemara notes: And it is necessary to learn about repentance both in the case of an individual and in the case of a community. The reason is that if we had learned this idea only with regard to an individual, one might have thought that he has the option to repent only because his sin is not publicized. But in the case of a community, whose sin is publicized, one might say that the community cannot repent. And likewise, if we had learned this idea only with regard to a community, one might have said that their repentance is accepted because their prayers are more numerous than those of an individual, and they are heard before God. But in the case of an individual, whose merit is not as strong, one might say that he is not able to repent. Therefore, it is necessary to teach both cases.”
